rationale: The exposure receipt answers the child question and narrows the consequence of the VerifyLeader finding without touching its mechanism. One trial is only one phase of the peers' randomized election timers, so the same measurement is submitted as a successor that repeats the interrupted case twelve times and the control twice; a local dry run of that harness (native feedback, not retained evidence) produced the same separation in all twelve trials, with the last confirmation at 45-49ms and the first competing leader at 58-126ms, so the retained run should either confirm the ordering or hand back a witness of the overlap.

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution (check 472bda105c83403b88d41a4b39596b6f, exit 0, tests_passed, 4 parsed events, 0 parse errors). Comparison 0 holds and is complete on result index 1, admitted by the interrupted baseline at index 0: with only the nonvoter on its side, the cut-off leader obtained eleven confirmations in a row, the last at 59ms after the partition, and the detached voters' leader first appeared at 121ms, so confirmation_precedes_peer_leader is true and confirmations_after_peer_leader is zero. Comparison 1 holds and is complete on result index 3, admitted by the control baseline at index 2: with the nonvoter also cut off the leader obtained no confirmation at all, while the detached leader appeared at 133ms and the nonvoter's term had already moved to 3. The measurement therefore answers the child question in the direction that narrows the consequence: in this configuration the confirmation window is closed by the cut-off leader's own lease before a competing leader can be elected, so the successful confirmations never coexisted with a newer leader, and no stale read was demonstrated. The reason is the timer relation the configuration enforces: ValidateConfig keeps LeaderLeaseTimeout at or below HeartbeatTimeout, which is at or below ElectionTimeout, the cut-off leader's lease expires one LeaderLeaseTimeout after its last successful voter contact, and the detached voters cannot even begin an election until their own heartbeat timers expire and then need an election round on top of that. The parent finding is unaffected in substance: the confirmation is still satisfied by an acknowledgement from a server that cannot vote, so it remains unsound as evidence of majority contact, which is what the documented read path relies on; what changes is that with these timer relations the unsound confirmation does not overlap a competing leader, so the stale-read consequence is not supported by this evidence.

knowledge.assertion: The confirmation on a leader cut off from the other voters depends on the nonvoter's acknowledgement; the control without it obtained no confirmation.

counterevidence: The separation is measured from a stable cluster, where the followers' timers had just been reset by the leader's own heartbeats. A partition applied while a follower was already campaigning (a node whose timer expired earlier, or a restarting follower with a fresh timer) would start the competing election earlier, and with the tightest measured margin (last confirmation 46ms against a competing leader at 58ms) that phase is not obviously excluded.

The competing leader is detected by polling the two detached voters every 5ms, so first_peer_leader_ms is an upper bound on when that leader appeared; the true appearance could be up to one poll interval earlier, which moves the two moments closer, though not past each other in the observed trials.
No application read is served in this harness; the measurement bounds when a competing leader can exist relative to the confirmation, not what an application would return.
limitations: One interrupted trial and one control are retained here; the twelve-trial successor is submitted because a single phase cannot bound a randomized-timer relation.
Only the captured in-memory timer values were used; the ordering argument is about the enforced relation between them rather than about these specific numbers.
The control confirms that without the nonvoter's acknowledgement no confirmation is possible, but it does not by itself measure the lease expiry, which is read from the leader's stepping down.

scope.description: Fourteen trials in total on real four-voter clusters with one voter demoted to nonvoter: twelve interrupted trials in which the leader is partitioned together with the nonvoter, and two controls in which the leader is partitioned alone. Each trial polls the exported verification path while the cut-off leader is confirmable, then watches until the detached voters report their own leader, and reports both moments on one clock with the competing leader's commit index and the cut-off leader's applied index.
assumptions: Each trial starts from a stable cluster with an elected leader and freshly heartbeated followers, so the trial-to-trial variation comes from the randomized election timers and scheduling rather than from a disturbed cluster.
Captured in-memory timeouts are used; the enforced relation LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout is a property of the configuration and is reported through the timeline.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses and stops as soon as the leader is no longer confirmable.
excluded: No partition during an already-running election attempt is exercised, so the adverse phase is not covered by this basis.
No application-level read, no on-disk store, no network transport and no synthetic request injection.

experiment.prefix: Unchanged from the predecessor harness apart from repetition: each trial builds a fresh real four-voter cluster, demotes one follower to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits for the configuration to show it without a vote, verifies the healthy leader once, applies one command, applies the partition, polls the verification path every 5ms while the leader reports Leader, stops when it is no longer confirmable or steps down, then watches for up to 3s until one of the two detached voters reports Leader, has it commit one entry, and emits one summary event per trial. Only the TestAssurance-prefixed test is selected and no production file is modified.

comparisons.description: Across the interrupted trials the last successful confirmation precedes the detached voters' leader; a violation would be a witness that the confirmation window overlapped a competing leader.
Both controls obtain no confirmation before stepping down.

experiment.revision_reason: Same question and same comparisons, changed basis: the predecessor ran one interrupted trial and one control, which cannot bound a relation that depends on the phase of the peers' randomized election timers. This revision repeats the interrupted case twelve times and the control twice, one fresh cluster per trial, keeping the same event shape, identity field and assertions so a violation is reported as a witness of an overlap rather than as an inconclusive result.
